## Coherence diagnostic — 11 categories

### (a) Repeated quotations
**Finding:** DMA 7, 702a17–19 ("the organic parts are suitably prepared by the affections, these again by desire, and desire by imagination") appeared verbatim in §1 (line 85) AND §4 (line 114).

**Fix applied:** §4's instance converted to a parenthetical reference back to the locus, with the four-stage relation expanded discursively rather than quoted. §1 retains the full quote as architectural anchor.

### (b) Transition seams
**Finding:** Zero forbidden back-reference patterns ("§1.4 has already…", "as we have seen at…", "in the previous subsection") detected at subsection boundaries.
**Fix applied:** None needed. The independent per-subsection generation appears to have inherently avoided forbidden back-references since each subsection has no prior-section context.

### (c) Terminology drift
**Finding:** Zero retired terms (dual-trace, "pathos feedback loop", resonant mood/tonality/trace). Two "faculty of X" instances appear at line 85, both INSIDE verbatim Aristotle quotation (`(De Anima, III.10, 433b13-18)`) using Smith/Barnes' translation; not real violations.
**Fix applied:** None.

### (d) Author imbalance
**Findings (corrected after diagnostic regex fix):**

| Author | Mentions in body |
|---|---:|
| Aristotle | 12+ |
| Heidegger | 5+ |
| Gross | **17** (across §§1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) |
| Caston | 0 |
| Frede | 0 |
| Gibson | 0 |
| Hawhee | 0 |
| Nussbaum | 0 |
| O'Gorman | 0 |
| Rickert | 0 |

**Gross presence achieved by pipeline:** 17 mentions distributed across §§1 (1), 4 (1), 5 (1), 6 (3), 7 (2), 8 (6), 9 (3). The corpus-index injection at retrieval time + the Source E verbatim quotes in the prelude + the per-subsection deltas worked. Initial diagnostic erroneously reported "0 Gross mentions" due to a regex bug that didn't match `(Gross, ``Introduction,'' in \textit{Heidegger and Rhetoric}, 2005, p.~X)` format.

**Secondary scholarship gaps (Caston, Frede, Hawhee, Nussbaum, O'Gorman, Rickert):** These authors' deployment was specified in subsection 2's delta (Nussbaum + Hawhee + O'Gorman on phantasia) but the LLM defaulted to inline narrative without explicit citation. Manual review recommended.

**Fix applied:** None for Gross (achieved). Secondary-scholarship gaps deferred to manual revision.

### (e) Bekker citation density
**Findings:**
- 46 Bekker locus references throughout the file.
- 0 "Aristotle, ..., p. X" formulations (Bekker compliance for Aristotle).
- **4 `[PAGE NEEDED]` markers** at lines 116, 129, 156, 171 — all citing `(Heidegger 2009, *Basic Concepts of Aristotelian Philosophy*, p. [PAGE NEEDED])` for pathos-as-altering claims.

**Fix applied:** None — page numbers require manual verification against the BCAP edition. Content of each marker:
- L116: Heidegger BCAP §17–18 on pathos as motion-and-cause-of-motion (~pp. 130–140)
- L129: same citation reused in §5 doxa-gate context (~pp. 130–140)
- L156: same in §6 hexis bivalence context (~pp. 122–128 area covers technē-hexis)
- L171: same in §7 pathetic-loop context (~pp. 133–138 covers Stimmung)

**Note:** Each occurrence has surrounding inline narrative that paraphrases the BCAP claim, so removing the [PAGE NEEDED] citation entirely is also viable.

### (f) BT/BCAP citation compliance
**Finding:** 0 BT references lack `§/H.X`. 1 BCAP reference lacks `p. X` (line 86 — inside running prose, not a parenthetical citation). All formal parenthetical BCAP citations include page numbers.
**Fix applied:** None.

### (g) Heidegger deferral footnote
**Finding:** Present at end of §8 (line ~178), well-formed: "The Heideggerian development of these themes…is the subject of the subsequent chapter on rhetoric, attunement, and ambient persuasion, in which Heidegger's account is brought into conversation with Rickert's *Ambient Rhetoric*, Burke's *A Grammar of Motives*, and Gross's *Heidegger and Rhetoric* and *Uncomfortable Situations*."
**Fix applied:** None — already present. Initial diagnostic missed it due to keyword search; corrected on second look.

### (h) Heading hierarchy
**Finding:** 8 `\subsubsection*{...}` blocks + 1 `\subsection*{Development Note}` block. Matches spec exactly. §9 used `\subsection*{}` despite buildSubsectionPrompt mandating `\subsubsection*{}` — the LLM correctly picked up the workflow convention from the delta context.
**Fix applied:** None.

### (i) Forbidden phrases
**Finding:** Zero hits for: "the user", "the reader", "this chapter", "the chapter", "underwrites", "rests on", "supplies the canonical", "to reiterate", "as we have discussed", "as we will see", "I should clarify here", "before we can analyze".
**Fix applied:** None — clean.

### (j) Work-in-narrative / locus-in-parens convention
**Finding:** 1 inline "at *Work* I.1, 123a1" formulation detected.
**Fix applied:** None — minor; flagged for manual review if needed.

### (k) Coinage compliance
**Finding:** Italicization of coinages (`\textit{resonant kinēsis}`, `\textit{resonant aisthēma}`, `\textit{resonant epithymia}`, `\textit{pathetic} loop`, `\textit{technē}-hexis`, `\textit{praxis}-hexis`) consistent across subsections; all instances italicized as units.
**Fix applied:** None.

## Items deferred to manual revision

1. **`[PAGE NEEDED]` × 4** — BCAP page numbers for pathos-as-altering citations at lines 116, 129, 156, 171. Either fill from BCAP (likely §17–18, ~pp. 130–140) or remove the citation in favor of the inline narrative attribution already present in each location.

2. **Word count overshoot (+31% aggregate)** — uniform across all 9 subsections. If subsection-scale word adherence matters for the dissertation, three remediation paths exist:
   - Manual trim per subsection (highest fidelity, ~30 min)
   - Add `exceeds-word-target` check to `investigateV1` (Phase 5 enhancement) so v2 fires on overshoot
   - Strengthen `buildSubsectionPrompt` length directive (Phase 4 enhancement)

3. **Secondary scholarship deployment** — Caston, Frede, Gibson, Hawhee, Nussbaum, O'Gorman, Rickert have 0 explicit citations despite being specified in §2's delta. Manual insertion using their corpus chunks (available in `corpus/rhetorical_ontology/`) may be desired.

4. **Gross deployment context** — though present 17 times, the user indicated wanting to manually review Gross integration per [[feedback-gross-advisor-citation-rigor]]. Lines 156, 171, 184 (×6), 186 are the primary Gross deployments and merit close reading.

5. **Optional minor item** — 1 inline "at *Work* I.1, 123a1" locus formulation could be converted to parenthetical per work-in-narrative convention.

## Comparison handoff metrics (versionA vs B vs C)

| Metric | versionA (rolling, no Source E) | versionB (rolling + Source E) | versionC (per-subsection + coherence) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Body word count | ~6,968 | ~7,165 | 9,017 |
| Gross body citations | 0 | 0 | 17 |
| `[PAGE NEEDED]` markers | 7 | 4 | 4 |
| "the user" instances | 4 | 2 | 0 |
| `pipelineHealth` | clean | clean | clean per subsection |
| Revision iterations | n/a (timeout) | n/a (timeout) | 0 per subsection |
| Generation wall-clock | ~7 hours | ~7 hours | ~37 minutes (9 × ~4 min sequential) |
| Approximate cost | ~$20 | ~$25 | ~$3–5 |

**versionC's most significant improvements over A/B:**
1. **Gross 17× vs 0×** — the per-subsection architecture + Source E injection finally cleared the advisor-rigor blocker (was the load-bearing concern of both A/B).
2. **"the user" zero** — subsection-mode's stricter prompt eliminated the residual second-person artifacts.
3. **Generation time 1/10th** — independent per-subsection runs parallelize well (foreground sequential here, but parallel-capable).
4. **Cost 1/5th** — shorter prompts per call + no rolling-context overhead.

**versionC's most significant regressions vs A/B:**
1. **+26% body word count** — pipeline overshoot not corrected by v2.
2. **`[PAGE NEEDED]` count unchanged** at 4 — the citation-resolution issue is corpus-level, not pipeline-architecture-level.
3. **Block-quote use leaner** than A/B (versionC has 2 spec-required block-quotes from §4's deltas; A/B had more via rolling-context's accumulated context).
